output.reason: The linked PR [ev-1acb9af98d76] says AWSProvider already had a `prefix` field, but only Parameter Store used it. The PR makes the Secrets Manager provider apply it too [ev-b2fe4d3529c1]. The validator found spec.provider.aws.prefix in the schema of both releases [ev-9889c9b8706d][ev-e08924afdc47]. So the only stores whose behaviour changes are AWS Secrets Manager stores (SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore) that already set prefix, because the field was ignored before and is now applied. The proposed condition "spec.provider.aws set" is too broad (it flags every AWS store) and also too narrow (it misses ClusterSecretStore).

correction.statement: In 0.16.0 the AWS Secrets Manager provider starts using AWSProvider.prefix (spec.provider.aws.prefix), which before only Parameter Store used. Exposed: any SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore that uses the AWS provider with service SecretsManager and already sets spec.provider.aws.prefix.
